name: Home First Finance Company India Ltd
tagline: High-quality affordable-housing financier — 25.7% AUM growth, 4.2% ROA, stable asset quality, PE promoters gradually exiting into strength — but a well-covered Rs 12,400 Cr mid-cap in a crowded space, not an under-the-radar multibagger
business_overview: Affordable-housing NBFC-HFC lending to first-time home buyers in the informal/self-employed segment, largely tier-2/3 markets, using a tech-driven underwriting/collections model. Competes with Aavas Financiers, Aptus Value Housing, Aadhar Housing and traditional HFCs/banks.
fundamentals_table: Rs 16,938 Cr, +25.7% YoY (Q1 FY27); disbursements +31% YoY
P/B compressed to ~2.84x (per a Mar-2026 community post) vs. a stated peer median ~4.1x
fundamentals_narrative: A genuinely well-run affordable-housing lender: consistent 25%+ AUM growth, improving ROA, and stable delinquencies through a period when some HFC/NBFC peers have seen pockets of stress. Nothing here contradicts the quality story. The question is not quality but scale and crowd — at Rs 12,400 Cr market cap in a segment with several well-covered listed comparables, this reads as a steady compounder rather than an overlooked opportunity.
sentiment_summary: VP thread (topic 63826, 44-47 posts, last active May 2026) shows sustained, unremarkable-in-a-good-way engagement: a mid-2024 update noting AUM crossing Rs 10,000 Cr with 34.8% YoY growth and management guiding 30%+ growth to continue; a Nov 2024 post flagging a promoter (True North/Aether) + Orange Capital block-deal sale of 14.7% at a modest discount to CMP, explicitly framed by the poster as reducing overhang risk, not distress; a Jan 2025 QIP (Rs 1,250 Cr) to fund growth; and a Mar 2026 post noting further True North/Aether stake reduction with current P/B (2.84x) called out as significantly below the peer median (4.1x). No red-flag-type posts (fraud, auditor resignation, promoter pledge) found anywhere in the thread history.
community_signal: Consistently constructive; the recurring theme is gradual, orderly private-equity promoter exit (True North, Aether — original VC/PE backers from the pre-IPO cap table) rather than any operational concern, alongside a live 'cheap vs. peers on P/B' argument as of early 2026.
bse_notes: No SEBI/fraud order; no going-concern issue. Promoter-group stake reduction (True North, Aether) is a planned PE-investor exit, not a distress signal — flagged by the community as reducing overhang, not creating risk. No red_flag_tier.
bull_case: Sustained 25%+ AUM growth with improving ROA (4.2%) and stable asset quality through Q1 FY27
P/B (~2.84x) below the community's cited peer median (~4.1x) as of the most recent thread update — a real relative-value argument
PE-promoter (True North/Aether) stake reduction is orderly/gradual, removing a future overhang rather than signalling distress
bear_case: Rs 12,400 Cr mid-cap in a well-covered, competitive affordable-HFC space (Aavas, Aptus, Aadhar Housing) — no evident under-the-radar edge
Growth (25-30% AUM) is genuinely good but not exceptional enough on its own to justify a 10x-in-2-3-years re-rating case at this scale
No unique moat beyond execution quality — underwriting/collections tech is replicable and several peers run similar playbooks

four_box.note: tailwind yes (structural affordable-housing/first-time-buyer credit penetration in tier-2/3 India, a genuine multi-year theme). tam weak (Rs 12,400 Cr mid-cap already; a 10x would require becoming one of India's largest HFCs, a stretch given competitive intensity). moat weak (good execution, no structural pricing power/switching cost). valuation weak (cheap vs. peers per the community, but not cheap in absolute terms at ~2.84x P/B for a 14.5% ROE lender). Score 2.5 -> 'neither' per the decision table (relative-value argument alone isn't the written 'valuation: yes' exception, since it's a relative not absolute cheapness case).

verdict_reasoning: External-lead (tier 4.5, @StocksAndStoics). No live-theme match in active_themes.json (affordable housing finance is not a listed theme). four_box score 2.5, no written exception taken (the peer-relative cheapness argument doesn't rise to a clean 'valuation: yes'), so thesis_fit stays 'neither'.

Conviction Medium: this is a genuinely high-quality, well-run lender with clean community sentiment and no governance flags — the size and crowded-space math, not business quality, is what caps the thesis at 'neither'.
No red_flag_tier, no revisit flag. A legitimate 'buy the quality compounder' name outside the scope of this open-mcap-multibagger screen's mandate.
disclaimer: This is independent research for informational purposes only, not investment advice.

market_expectation.implied_growth_cagr: ~2.9x P/B on a 16% ROE affordable-housing financier implies the market expects ~25% AUM growth to persist; fair at 2.5-3x P/B needs ROE held at 16-18% with AUM +20-25%
market_expectation.our_fy27_estimate: AUM +25%, ROA ~3.8-4.2%, EPS +20-25%; asset quality stable (GNPA ~1.8%)
market_expectation.our_fy28_estimate: growth durability in a crowded affordable-housing space; PE-promoter overhang gradually clearing
market_expectation.gap_basis: a well-covered Rs 12,400 Cr mid-cap; consensus already models the 25% AUM growth and stable ROA, so the price roughly reflects our path
market_expectation.data_caveat: no broker consensus; implied path is a reverse-P/E estimate + screener.in forward figures + VP thread view

quality_metrics.note: Housing-finance NBFC - leverage/coverage/FCF/capex metrics not meaningful. Based on ROE ~16% (13%->16% FY23->FY26), ROA ~4.2%, GNPA 1.80% / NNPA 1.40% with stable asset quality, net profit margin ~28%. capex_efficiency set neutral as not applicable.

track_record.note: FY24 (+45%/ROE 16%), FY25 (+33%/16%) and FY26 (+25%/16%) each cleared both filters (ROE used in place of ROCE for a lender). Pre-FY24 ROE was 13%; the growth-with-return record covers the last three years.
